specs.label: Overlay launcher ▸ Settings
specs.note: The shell overlay launcher (title 'Settings') mounts the settings overlay panel (features/settings/SettingsPanel). Once mounted, the .setlaunch bar with its three window buttons and a status readout appears. This is the entry point to every settings surface, so it runs first and leaves the panel open for the window-open specs that follow.

specs.label: .setlaunch ▸ Setting (open the Setting-menu window)
specs.note: First .setlaunch button opens the FloatingWindow hosting the data-driven menu renderer (title = the active tab, default 'Setting'). In local mode the body shows 'settings service unavailable' because the catalogue is bridge-served; the window itself still opens. Relies on settings.panel.open having mounted the panel.

specs.label: .setlaunch ▸ Edit All… (open the Advanced Settings table window)
specs.note: Second .setlaunch button opens the 'PyMOL Advanced Settings' FloatingWindow. The title bar renders regardless of phase; the body shows the table when ready or 'settings service unavailable' in local mode.

specs.label: .setlaunch ▸ Lighting (open the Lighting Settings window)
specs.note: Third .setlaunch button opens the 'Lighting Settings' FloatingWindow. Title bar renders regardless of phase; body shows presets+sliders when ready or the unavailable notice in local mode.

specs.label: FloatingWindow ▸ × close button
specs.note: The window's × (.flwin__close) fires onClose, which sets the panel's open state back to null and unmounts the window. Enters with the Lighting window still open (from the prior spec; resetApp does not close FloatingWindows because focus has moved to the command line).

specs.label: .setlaunch ▸ Setting toggles its window closed on second click
specs.note: Each .setlaunch button toggles its own window: clicking 'Setting' with no window open opens the menu window; clicking it again closes it (setOpen(open==='menu'?null:'menu')). Self-contained: opens then closes within the trigger.

specs.label: Setting-menu window ▸ tab: Setting
specs.note: First tab switches the renderer to the harvested Setting menu subtree (244 leaves). Tabs only render when the catalogue is ready, so this is bridge-gated.

specs.label: Setting-menu window ▸ tab: Display
specs.note: Second tab switches the renderer to the Display menu subtree (Sequence, Internal GUI, Stereo, Zoom/Clip, Background, Quality, Grid, …).

specs.label: Setting-menu window ▸ tab: Mouse
specs.note: Third tab switches the renderer to the Mouse menu subtree (Selection Mode radios, N-button motion presets, Virtual Trackball, Roving Origin).

specs.label: Setting-menu window ▸ tab: Scene
specs.note: Fourth tab switches the renderer to the Scene menu subtree (Scenes…, Next/Previous, Recall/Store/Clear F-keys, Buttons check, Cache commands).

specs.label: Setting-menu window ▸ get_menudata provenance chip
specs.note: The .setmenu__source chip carries the harvest provenance in its title (menudata source + generator path). Hovering surfaces the tooltip; the chip only renders in the ready menu window.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Auto-Zoom New Objects (check → auto_zoom)
specs.note: A top-level check row toggles auto_zoom via cmd.set. The mark (✓) and aria-checked flip against the LIVE value read back from the settings tap.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Auto-Remove Hydrogens (check → auto_remove_hydrogens)
specs.note: Top-level check toggles auto_remove_hydrogens; mark and aria-checked track the live value.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Show Text (Esc) (check → text)
specs.note: Top-level check toggles the 'text' setting (overlay text display).

specs.label: Setting ▸ Overlay Text (check → overlay)
specs.note: Top-level check toggles the 'overlay' setting.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Label (submenu expand/collapse)
specs.note: Top-level submenus render collapsed (useState(depth>0)); clicking the header expands it, revealing the nested radio groups (label_size, label_font_id, …). First .setmenu__submenu header on the Setting tab is 'Label'.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Label ▸ Size ▸ radio (label_size)
specs.note: Inside the expanded Label ▸ Size radio group, choosing a member writes label_size via cmd.set; the ● dot follows the live value, not a local selection. Second radio in the label_size group ('14 Point').

specs.label: Setting ▸ Edit All… (command → settings_edit_all_dialog hook)
specs.note: The first command row runs the settings_edit_all_dialog hook that SettingsPanel binds itself (localHooks), switching the window to the Advanced Settings table. Proves the panel's own toolkit-seam wiring. First .setmenu__row--command on the Setting tab.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… (command → shortcut_menu_edit_dialog hook)
specs.note: Second command row targets the shortcut_menu_edit_dialog seam. If no feature has registered that hook it renders DISABLED with an explanatory tooltip (hookNote); if a feature owns it, it opens. Verifies the disabled-vs-live hook path either way. Second .setmenu__row--command.

specs.label: Setting ▸ Colors… (command → edit_colors_dialog hook)
specs.note: Third command row targets the edit_colors_dialog seam (owned by the colors feature if registered, otherwise disabled). Third .setmenu__row--command.

specs.label: Mouse ▸ Selection Mode ▸ radio (mouse_selection_mode)
specs.note: On the Mouse tab the Selection Mode radio group writes mouse_selection_mode (Atoms/Residues/Chains/…). Choosing a member writes the setting and moves the ● to the live value. Third radio ('Chains').

specs.label: Display ▸ Stereo Mode ▸ command (do: stereo …)
specs.note: On the Display tab, Stereo Mode holds 'do'-type command leaves (Anaglyph/Cross-Eye/…/off) that run a raw command line rather than writing a single setting. Exercises the command-node 'do' action branch of the renderer. Requires expanding the Stereo Mode submenu first (nth chosen after expansion).

specs.label: Scene ▸ command (call: scene recall/next)
specs.note: On the Scene tab the top-level command rows (Scenes…, Next, Previous, Append, …) are 'call'/'hook' leaves. Exercises a Scene-menu command leaf. First .setmenu__row--command (Scenes… hook) or Next; verifies command dispatch from the panel-hosted Scene menu.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Filter (substring narrows rows)
specs.note: Typing into the filter box runs filterSettings over name+help and re-windows the row list; the count 'N / total' drops. Bridge-gated because the 779-row catalogue is bridge-served.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Filter (regex)
specs.note: The filter accepts a regex (matched over both columns). '^cartoon_' should narrow to the cartoon_* family.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ value cell (type + Enter commits a write)
specs.note: A non-boolean value cell is a text field: editing the draft and pressing Enter blurs and commits via source.write(cmd.set)+read-back; the cell snaps to the value PyMOL actually holds. Filter to sphere_scale first to get one editable row.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ value cell (Escape discards the draft)
specs.note: Escape in a value cell resets the draft to null (no write). The cell reverts to the live shown value.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ boolean value cell (checkbox toggle)
specs.note: A boolean setting renders its value cell as a checkbox that writes 1/0 through cmd.set. Filter to a boolean setting (orthoscopic) first.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Reset (⟲ → cmd.unset restores default)
specs.note: The per-row ⟲ button calls source.reset (cmd.unset), restoring the compiled default; it is disabled when the value already equals the default. Set a non-default value first so the button is enabled.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Scope: global (default)
specs.note: The scope Select offers global/object/object-state/atom/atom-state/bond. 'global' is the default and shows no object/selection sub-control.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Scope: object (reveals Object selector)
specs.note: Choosing 'object' reveals a second Select of object names; reading a whole object scope then re-reads every visible setting for that object.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Scope: object-state (reveals Object + State)
specs.note: 'object-state' reveals both the Object selector and a numeric State input; per-state values are read for the chosen object+state.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Scope: atom (reveals Selection input + overrides)
specs.note: 'atom' reveals the Selection text input and switches the value cells to write-only; the OverridesView strip reports what a selection carries via cmd.iterate.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Scope: atom-state (reveals Selection + State + AtomStateStrip)
specs.note: 'atom-state' writes go through cmd.alter_state (atomSettings.ts) rather than cmd.set; it reveals Selection + State and the AtomStateStrip that reports the atom count alter_state answered (overrides cannot be listed back).

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Scope: bond (reveals Selection; writes via set_bond)
specs.note: 'bond' writes through cmd.set_bond (cmd.set with a selection silently no-ops at bond level); reveals the Selection input with the bond placeholder and a per-bond overrides read via cmd.get_bond.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Selection input (atom scope)
specs.note: Typing a selection under the atom scope drives the OverridesView read-back (cmd.iterate over the selection).

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ State number input (object-state scope)
specs.note: The numeric State input (object-state / atom-state scopes) selects which state's values are read; it clamps to >=1.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ virtualised body scroll
specs.note: The 779-row list is windowed; scrolling .setadv__body updates the visible slice (translateY) so different rows enter the DOM. Verifies the virtualisation without a filter.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Reinitialize ▸ Everything (arms, then runs)
specs.note: 'Everything' is destructive (deletes every object AND resets settings), so the first click arms it (label -> 'Everything?') and a second confirms and calls cmd.reinitialize('everything'). Two clicks in the trigger cover both steps.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Reinitialize ▸ Everything (arm state only)
specs.note: A single click on the destructive 'Everything' entry only ARMS it — the label gains a '?' and the button gets .is-armed — without running anything. Confirms the confirm-first guard the Qt File menu lacks.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Reinitialize ▸ Original Settings
specs.note: Non-destructive: runs cmd.reinitialize('original_settings') then re-bootstraps the catalogue. Note the label/word mismatch — 'Original Settings' maps to the original_settings word.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Reinitialize ▸ Stored Settings
specs.note: Runs cmd.reinitialize('settings') ('Stored Settings' label maps to the settings word) then re-bootstraps.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ Reinitialize ▸ Store Current Settings
specs.note: Runs cmd.reinitialize('store_defaults') to make the current settings the ones 'Stored Settings' restores.

specs.label: Advanced table ▸ footer defaults/ranges provenance
specs.note: The footer states where defaults + ranges came from (catalogue.meta.defaultsSource / minMaxNote) or warns if unavailable. A passive provenance readout, present once the catalogue loads.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ Preset: Default
specs.note: Applies the 17-setting Default preset (main.py:69-137) by writing each named setting through source.write. Bridge-gated (needs the catalogue to map names to metas).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ Preset: Metal
specs.note: Applies the Metal preset's setting block.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ Preset: Plastic
specs.note: Applies the Plastic preset's setting block.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ Preset: Rubber
specs.note: Applies the Rubber preset's setting block.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ Preset: X-Ray
specs.note: Applies the X-Ray preset's 17-setting block.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ ambient (number field)
specs.note: The authoritative number field for ambient (0..1); onChange writes unclamped through cmd.set and reads back.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ ambient (range slider)
specs.note: The ambient slider (#light-ambient) is a hint that writes through cmd.set on change; the number field is authoritative and both re-read.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ reflect (number field)
specs.note: Number field for reflect (-1..1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ direct (number field; label 'direct (+reflect)')
specs.note: The 'direct (+reflect)' row's setting name is 'direct' (the parenthetical is split off, main.py:227); number field range -1..1.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ spec_direct (number field)
specs.note: Number field for spec_direct (0..1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ spec_direct_power (number field)
specs.note: Number field for spec_direct_power (0..100, step 1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ light_count (number field)
specs.note: Number field for light_count (1..8, step 1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ edit_light (number field)
specs.note: Number field for edit_light (1..7, step 1) — which placeable light is being edited.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ spec_count (number field)
specs.note: Number field for spec_count (-1..8, step 1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ shininess (number field)
specs.note: Number field for shininess (0..100).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ shininess (range slider)
specs.note: The shininess slider (#light-shininess) writes through cmd.set on change.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ spec_reflect (number field)
specs.note: Number field for spec_reflect (-0.01..1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ specular (number field)
specs.note: Number field for specular (0..1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ specular_intensity (number field; label '=specular')
specs.note: The 'specular_intensity (=specular)' row's setting name is 'specular_intensity' (parenthetical split off); range 0..1.

specs.label: Lighting ▸ ambient_occlusion_mode (number field)
specs.note: Number field for ambient_occlusion_mode (0..2, step 1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ ambient_occlusion_scale (number field)
specs.note: Number field for ambient_occlusion_scale (1..50, step 1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ ambient_occlusion_smooth (number field)
specs.note: Number field for ambient_occlusion_smooth (1..20, step 1).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ power (number field, ray-trace only)
specs.note: Number field for power (1..10).

specs.label: Lighting ▸ reflect_power (number field, ray-trace only)
specs.note: Number field for reflect_power (1..10).
